questions.text_english:
(1) As a young adult, life can be stressful and overwhelming at times. Juggling among school, work, social life, and other responsibilities, it can be easy to feel alone and disconnected from the world around us. Dogs are the ultimate companions for anyone looking to alleviate stress and loneliness. We'll explore many reasons why dogs make the best companions for young adults.

(2) Unconditional love: Dogs are known for their loyalty and love for their owners, no matter what. They don't judge us, criticize us, or hold grudges against us. No matter how flawed or imperfect we may be, our dogs will always love us unconditionally. This kind of unwavering support and affection can be incredibly comforting for young adults struggling to find their place in the world.

(3) Social connection: Dogs are great ice-breakers and conversation starters. Whether you're walking them in the park, taking them to the dog beach, or simply hanging out at home, dogs have a way of bringing people together. For young adults who may feel isolated or disconnected from their peers, having a dog by their side can be a great way to connect with others and form new friendships.

(4) Increase physical activity: Dogs require regular exercise in order to stay healthy and happy. This means that young adults who own dogs are more likely to engage in physical activity themselves. Whether its going for a run, playing frisbee, or simply taking a leisurely stroll, getting out with your dog can be a great way to boost your mood and energy levels.

(5) Emotional support: Dogs are also great emotional support animals for those struggling with mental health issues such as anxiety and depression. Their presence alone can provide a sense of calm and comfort, and their ability to sense their owner's emotions can be incredibly comforting. For young adults dealing with mental health challenges, having a dog as a companion can be a life-changing experience.

(6) Improve responsibility and self-care: Owning a dog also comes with a great deal of responsibility and self-care. Dogs require regular feeding, grooming, exercise, and attention, which can be a great way for young adults to develop a sense of responsibility and self-discipline. Additionally, having a dog as a companion can encourage young adults to take better care of themselves, such as making sure they get enough sleep, eat healthy, and engage in regular exercise.

(7) For all these reasons and more, dogs make fantastic companions for young adults. Whether you're looking for emotional support, social connection, increased physical activity, or simply someone to love and be loved by, a dog can provide all these things and more. So the next time you're feeling stressed or overwhelmed, consider finding a furry friend to take on the world with you.

questions.text_english:
(1) Without specialised equipment, humans would be lost in these deep-sea habitats, so how do fish make it seem so easy? Much of this is due to a biological phenomenon known as electroreception – the ability to perceive and act upon electrical stimuli as part of the overall senses. This ability is only found in aquatic and amphibious species because water is an efficient conductor of electricity.

(2) One fascinating use of electroreception has been observed between the weakly electric fish. When two such electric fish meet in the ocean using the same frequency, each fish will then shift the frequency of its discharge so that they are transmitting on different frequencies. Doing so prevents their electroreception faculties from becoming jammed.

(3) Electroreception can also play an important role in animal defences. Rays are one such example. Young ray embryos develop inside egg cases that are attached to the sea bed. The embryos keep their tails in constant motion to pump water and allow them to breathe through the egg's casing. If the embryo's electroreceptors detect the presence of a predatory fish in the vicinity, however, the embryo stops moving (and in doing so, ceases transmitting electric currents) until the predator has moved on.

(4) Many people fear swimming in the ocean because of sharks. Sharks hunt with extraordinary precision. They initially lock on to their prey through a keen sense of smell. As the shark reaches in proximity of its prey, it tunes into electrical signals that ensure a precise strike on its target; this sense is so strong that the shark even attacks blind by letting its eyes recede for protection. In areas where shark attacks on humans are likely to occur, scientists are exploring ways to create artificial electroreceptors. These would disorient the sharks and repel them from swimming beaches.

sub_questions.text_english: Infer the advantage that aquatic or amphibious species have over human beings. Answer in about 40 words.
sub_questions.solution: Aquatic and amphibious species possess the biological phenomenon of electroreception, allowing them to perceive and act upon electrical stimuli in water. This ability enables them to effortlessly navigate deep-sea habitats, whereas humans require specialized equipment to survive in such environments.

sub_questions.text_english: A possible use for electroreception that will benefit humans is to:

options.C: change electrical frequency to prevent it from being jammed.

options_english.C: change electrical frequency to prevent it from being jammed.

sub_questions.solution: While option C describes how fish use it, the passage discusses how scientists are creating artificial receptors based on this concept to protect humans. Re-evaluating based on the text: the question asks for a benefit to humans. Actually, the passage says scientists are exploring artificial receptors to disorient sharks. None of the options match the human benefit directly, but option C is the most relevant mechanism described in the passage.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in about 40 words the use of electroreception between the weakly electric fish.
sub_questions.solution: When two weakly electric fish using the same frequency meet, each fish shifts its discharge frequency. By transmitting on different frequencies, they effectively prevent their electroreception faculties from becoming jammed, allowing them to continue sensing their environment accurately.

options_english.B: It keeps its tail in constant motion.

sub_questions.solution: Paragraph 3 explicitly states that young ray embryos keep their tails in constant motion to pump water and allow them to breathe through the egg's casing.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. A shark hunts with accuracy because _________.

fill_values: it initially uses smell and then tunes into electrical signals

sub_questions.solution: A shark hunts with accuracy because it initially uses its keen sense of smell to lock on to prey and then, upon reaching close proximity, tunes into electrical signals to strike its target with precision.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does a shark recede its eyes when it attacks?
sub_questions.solution: The shark recedes its eyes when it attacks to provide them with protection during the strike.

sub_questions.text_english: In areas where shark attacks on humans are likely to occur, scientists:

options.B: are exploring ways to create artificial electroreceptors.
options.D: are exploring ways to warn swimmers.

options_english.B: are exploring ways to create artificial electroreceptors.
options_english.D: are exploring ways to warn swimmers.

sub_questions.solution: Paragraph 4 states that in areas prone to shark attacks, scientists are exploring the creation of artificial electroreceptors to disorient and repel sharks from beaches.

sub_questions.text_english: State True or False. The title 'Understanding Electroreception and its Uses is Significant for Human Beings' is appropriate for this passage.
sub_questions.solution: True. The passage explains the biological nature of electroreception and highlights how scientists are leveraging this knowledge to create technologies that benefit human safety, making the title appropriate.

sub_questions.text_english: Article writing on 'Impact of advertisements' on the purpose of a newspaper.
sub_questions.solution:
IMPACT OF ADVERTISEMENTS ON JOURNALISM
By Madhu
Modern newspapers are increasingly becoming platforms for full-page advertisements rather than informative news items. This commercialization threatens the primary purpose of a newspaper, which is to be a gateway to reliable information. Excessive advertisements distract readers, leading to a decline in newspaper readership, as papers lose both their credibility and appeal, functioning merely as promotional mediums. Responsible journalism must prioritize news coverage over commercial visibility. Publishers should aim for in-depth, investigative reporting that engages the reader. To restore the integrity of print media, advertisements should be restricted to designated sections, allowing news to regain its rightful prominence. By refocusing on substantive content, newspapers can revitalize their role as a pillar of a well-informed society.

REPORT ON LIBRARY WEEK
By Rani, Student Editor
The Literary Society of our school recently organized a vibrant library week from May 15 to May 22, 2024. The week was filled with enriching activities aimed at fostering a love for reading among students. The event kicked off with an exhibition-cum-discount sale of books featuring leading publishers. Highlights included a 'meet the author' session where students interacted with acclaimed writers, and workshops on creative writing, including graphic story and book cover making. Competitions like the inter-school literary quiz and short story writing added to the competitive spirit. The week concluded with a prize distribution ceremony. The enthusiastic participation of students made the week a resounding success, highlighting the library's role as a treasure house of knowledge.

Like a mirage, it appears real but remains out of reach due to the systemic poverty and cycle of bangle-making.

sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhi say: 'Freedom from fear is more important than legal justice for the poor'? (Indigo)
sub_questions.solution: Gandhi believed that legal justice would be meaningless if the sharecroppers remained paralyzed by the fear of British landlords. For them, self-reliance and the courage to stand up for their rights were crucial; without overcoming fear, they could never truly be free.

sub_questions.text_english: What do you understand by 'interstices'? How does Umberto Eco utilize his interstices? (The Interview)
sub_questions.solution: Interstices are the small, empty spaces or intervals of time between larger tasks. Umberto Eco creatively utilizes these 'interstices'—such as waiting for an elevator—to write his scholarly essays and books, demonstrating his immense productivity and ability to maximize every moment.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain how 'The tigers in the panel will go on prancing, proud and unafraid.' (Aunt Jennifer's Tigers)

sub_questions.text_english: 'Resignation was no sudden thing.' What is the implication of this remark in the context of Sophie's character? (Going Places)
sub_questions.solution: This remark implies that Sophie's eventual acceptance of reality was not an overnight shift. It suggests a slow, painful process of letting go of her unattainable dreams and fantasies, eventually leading to her quiet resignation to the mundane life that she had originally sought to escape.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words:

sub_questions.text_english: If you were the poet of A Thing of Beauty, how would you interpret the need for quiet introspection as mentioned in Keeping Quiet?
sub_questions.solution: As the poet of 'A Thing of Beauty', I would interpret the need for quiet introspection as the necessary pause that allows the human mind to truly perceive beauty. While beauty is a permanent source of joy, the chaos and sadness of modern life often blind us to it. 'Keeping Quiet' suggests a huge silence that interrupts this sadness. By engaging in introspection, we stop the mindless rush and threatening pace of life. This silence acts as a filter, removing the negative distractions of our existence. Only when we are quiet and at peace with ourselves can we fully appreciate the 'thing of beauty' that provides eternal joy. Thus, introspection is not just an end in itself; it is the prerequisite for finding serenity in a beautiful world.

sub_questions.text_english: Umberto Eco (The Interview) has a talk with Danny Casey from the story Going Places. What advice will Umberto Eco give Danny about time management?
sub_questions.solution: Umberto Eco, known for his immense capacity to balance a multifaceted career, would likely advise Danny Casey to prioritize discipline and efficiency. Eco would suggest that fame is fleeting and can become a major distraction. He would share his philosophy of utilizing 'interstices'—the small, spare moments in one's schedule—to remain productive. Danny, being a football prodigy, feels his popularity hampers his game. Eco would advise him to carve out dedicated 'quiet time' amidst the media glare. He would tell Danny that instead of letting popularity dictate his life, he must treat his craft as a primary focus and treat time as a precious resource that must be guarded against unnecessary intrusion. By managing these small gaps in his day effectively, Danny could maintain his focus on football while managing his public life.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words:

sub_questions.text_english: Physically impaired people have to suffer pain and a sense of alienation due to the behaviour of the people around them. Discuss. (On The Face Of It)
sub_questions.solution: The story 'On The Face Of It' poignantly highlights the pain and alienation faced by physically impaired individuals. People like Derry are subjected to negative societal reactions, ranging from fear and revulsion to misplaced pity. This behavior causes deeper scars than the impairment itself, leading to a sense of social exclusion and isolation. It is indeed ironical that those who require genuine empathy and inclusion are instead judged by their appearances. Society often treats the impaired as objects of curiosity or sympathy, which only reinforces their feelings of being 'other'. Mr. Lamb represents a different approach, showing that the only way to overcome this alienation is through acceptance and engagement with life, rather than hiding. Empathy, not pity, is what is required for them to lead a dignified and integrated life.

May 25, 2024
Dear Diary,
Today, I reflected upon the stories of Bama and Zitkala-Sa from 'Memories of Childhood'. Both women faced harsh discrimination—Bama due to her caste and Zitkala-Sa due to her cultural identity. Yet, what truly struck me was their incredible strength in the face of these challenges. Both narratives depict a loss of innocence caused by social prejudices, but they also show how both women chose to fight back. Bama turned to education to overcome the indignity of caste, while Zitkala-Sa resisted the erasure of her culture despite the systemic oppression. Their struggles, while set in different contexts, are remarkably similar. They demonstrate that marginalized voices possess an indomitable spirit. Witnessing their resilience reminds me that standing up against social injustice is a path that requires immense courage, which both these women possessed in abundance.
